R01.expected_answer: Grounds of arrest must be given in writing, in a language the arrestee understands, for every offence (IPC/BNS included), and at least 2 hours before production for remand. If not, the arrest and remand are illegal and he is entitled to release. Some High Courts apply this only to arrests made after 6 Nov 2025.
R01.key_authority_text: Outdated: Pankaj Bansal (2023) and Prabir Purkayastha (2024) required written grounds only under PMLA/UAPA, and Vihaan Kumar (2025) treated writing as ideal rather than mandatory. Current: Mihir Rajesh Shah v. State of Maharashtra, SC, 6 Nov 2025, 2025 INSC 1288 (Gavai CJI, Masih J). A Delhi HC Division Bench in Karan Singh v. State (NCT of Delhi), 2026:DHC:570-DB (reported 28 Jan 2026), held the written-grounds mandate "operates prospectively", but a later Delhi HC NDPS ruling rejected the prospective-only argument, so the Delhi HC is itself split.

trap_pair.outdated: Pankaj Bansal (2023) / Prabir Purkayastha (2024): written grounds required under PMLA/UAPA only

R02.expected_answer: No. A s.35 BNSS (old s.41A CrPC) notice must be served in a mode the statute prescribes; WhatsApp or email service is invalid. For offences punishable up to 7 years, a notice is the rule and arrest the exception. Arrest for non-compliance needs a validly served notice and recorded reasons.
R02.key_authority_text: Satender Kumar Antil v. CBI, SC, 2025 INSC 909 (Sundresh & Kotiswar Singh JJ), upholding the 21 Jan 2025 order. Satender Kumar Antil v. CBI (2022) 10 SCC 51. Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273. BNSS s.35 = CrPC s.41A.

R03.expected_answer: The officer must prepare an arrest memo attested by a witness and countersigned by the arrestee, inform a relative or friend, and let the arrestee meet an advocate during (not throughout) interrogation. Breach exposes officers to departmental action and contempt, and the State to public-law compensation. The BNSS equivalents are ss.36, 38 and 48.
R03.key_authority_text: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal (1997) 1 SCC 416. CrPC ss.41B/41D/50A = BNSS ss.36/38/48.

R05.expected_answer: Probably not. Default bail under s.187(3) BNSS (old s.167(2) CrPC) is lost once a charge-sheet in proper form is filed within 60/90 days. Pending further investigation against other accused does not revive it, and neither does failure to supply copies. Ritu Chhabaria's "incomplete charge-sheet" reasoning was put on hold in 2023; the CBI's review was dismissed in Aug 2025, but its practical reach is narrow.

R06.expected_answer: Yes. A first-time offender who has served one-third of the maximum sentence as an undertrial must be released on bond under s.479 BNSS; for theft (IPC 379, up to 3 years) that is 12 months. The Supreme Court held s.479 applies to undertrials whose cases were registered before 1 July 2024. It does not apply to offences punishable with death or life imprisonment.
R06.key_authority_text: In Re: Inhuman Conditions in 1382 Prisons, W.P.(C) 406/2013, SC order of 23 Aug 2024 (Hima Kohli & Sandeep Mehta JJ), 2024 LiveLaw (SC) 632. BNSS s.479 replaces CrPC s.436A (one-half rule).

R07.expected_answer: Under the 2025 guidelines, payment before defence evidence allows compounding with no cost. After defence evidence but before judgment the cost is 5%; in appeal or revision before the Sessions Court or High Court it is 7.5%; before the Supreme Court it is 10%. The court may suggest compounding. If the complainant resists, it can consider probation-type relief.

R12.expected_answer: Yes, it can be quashed. A breach of contract is not cheating unless there was dishonest intent at the very start, and criminal breach of trust needs entrustment. Where an FIR only dresses up a civil default, it and the charge-sheet can be quashed under s.482 CrPC (now s.528 BNSS). The Supreme Court imposed ₹50,000 costs on the State in a near-identical case.
R12.key_authority_text: Rikhab Birani v. State of U.P., SC, 16 Apr 2025, 2025 INSC 512 (Khanna CJI, Sanjay Kumar J).

authorities.label: Rikhab Birani v. State of U.P. (2025)

R13.expected_answer: The High Court may quash on settlement where the dispute is mainly civil, commercial or private and continuing would be futile. It should not do so for heinous offences or offences against society, such as serious economic fraud or sexual offences.
R13.key_authority_text: Parbatbhai Aahir v. State of Gujarat, SC 3-judge bench, 4 Oct 2017, (2017) 9 SCC 641. State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335. BNSS s.528 = CrPC s.482.

State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal (1990/92)

R14.expected_answer: Usually yes, if the FIR shows only failure to repay or a business loss without dishonest intent at the start. Courts deprecate using criminal law as a recovery tool, and the remedy lies in civil or arbitration proceedings.
R14.key_authority_text: Indian Oil Corp. v. NEPC India Ltd (2006) 6 SCC 736. Rikhab Birani v. State of U.P., 2025 INSC 512.

R15.expected_answer: Arrest is governed by s.35 BNSS and Arnesh Kumar: for offences up to 7 years, notice first and no automatic arrest. Social Action Forum (2018) withdrew Rajesh Sharma's Family Welfare Committee directions. In July 2025, however, a two-judge bench in Shivangi Bansal directed the Allahabad HC's FWC guidelines, with a 2-month cooling period and no arrest, to be implemented. That ruling does not reconcile with the larger bench, so the position is unsettled. Distant relatives can seek quashing of omnibus allegations.

R17.expected_answer: The prosecution must prove direct or indirect incitement, an intention to drive the deceased to suicide, and a proximate positive act. Harassment alone, without a live link to the suicide, is not enough. IPC 306 is now BNS 108.
R17.key_authority_text: Ude Singh v. State of Haryana, 25 Jul 2019, (2019) 17 SCC 301. Kumar @ Shiva Kumar v. State of Karnataka, SC, 1 Mar 2024, 2024 INSC 156, [2024] 3 SCR 329 (opinion by Bhuyan J): harassment allegations without "any positive action proximate to the time of occurrence" cannot sustain a s.306 IPC conviction.

R20.expected_answer: For pre-July 2024 conduct under IPC 375/376, consent is vitiated only if the promise was false from the start and directly influenced the decision; breaking a genuine promise is not rape. For conduct from 1 July 2024, BNS s.69 creates a separate offence of intercourse by deceitful means, including a false promise to marry made without intent to fulfil it (up to 10 years).
R20.key_authority_text: Pramod Suryabhan Pawar v. State of Maharashtra, SC, 21 Aug 2019, (2019) 9 SCC 608. BNS s.69 (India Code).

R22.expected_answer: Possibly. The sentencing court must actively collect mitigating material before imposing death: a psychological or psychiatric evaluation, a jail conduct report and a probation or background report. A rushed sentencing hearing without this is a ground for commutation or remand. The "rarest of rare" test from Bachan Singh still governs. IPC 302 is now BNS 103.
R22.key_authority_text: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980) 2 SCC 684. Manoj v. State of M.P., SC, 20 May 2022, (2023) 2 SCC 353, 2022 INSC 606.

R23.expected_answer: It depends on intention and the circumstances. A single blow in a sudden fight without premeditation or cruelty may fall under Exception 4 to s.300 IPC, making it culpable homicide not amounting to murder (s.304 IPC; BNS ss.101/105). The weapon, the body part struck and the force used are key.
R23.key_authority_text: Pulicherla Nagaraju v. State of A.P. (2006) 11 SCC 444. IPC 300/302/304 = BNS 101/103/105.

IPC 406 → BNS 316(2), which provides imprisonment "which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both", up from 3 years under the IPC (confirmed by AZB & Partners' BNS overview; India Code not opened).
